title: Six Heuristic Frameworks
intro: Heuristic evaluation isn't a last resort or a checklist. The mistake is using only Nielsen's ten and stopping at naming violations.

learn.title: Six lenses
learn.text:
**Norman — 7 principles:** big-picture “is it intuitive?”, physical or cross-device products
**Nielsen — 10 heuristics:** general usability review; the shared vocabulary
**Weinschenk & Barker — 20:** detailed guidelines including persuasion and emotion
**Tognazzini — first principles:** complex interaction; defaults, anticipation, autonomy
**Gerhardt-Powals — 10:** data-heavy, high-stakes screens; cognitive engineering
**Covert — IA heuristics:** navigation, findability, labelling, structure

One framework is a checklist; several are a toolkit.

try.q: You're reviewing a data-heavy trading screen. Which lens fits best?
try.explain: Cognitive engineering principles were written for high-stakes, information-dense displays.

learn.title: Norman's seven, as a starting point
learn.text:
• Use knowledge in the world and in the head
• Simplify the structure of tasks
• Make things visible — state, options, results
• Get the mappings right
• Exploit the power of constraints
• Design for error
• When all else fails, standardise

Good for asking whether something is intuitive at all, before you go looking for specific violations.

try.q: What is “design for error” an example of?
try.explain: Norman's list is the big-picture lens.

right.label: Toolkit use
items: Pick the lens for the problem
Explain the cost to the user

learn.title: Stop at the violation and you've stopped early
learn.text:
Naming the heuristic is the beginning. The useful output says **what it costs the user** and what to change.

And a navigation problem is better served by Covert's IA heuristics than by forcing it into Nielsen's ten — which is the point of keeping six frameworks to hand.

test.q: What is the common mistake with heuristic evaluation?
options: Using only Nielsen's ten and naming violations
Running it with too few reviewers
Applying it too early in design
test.explain: It becomes a checklist instead of research.

test.q: Which set includes persuasion and emotion?
test.explain: The most detailed of the six.

test.q: What is Nielsen's set best used for?
test.explain: It's the common language, not the only lens.

test.q: Which lens covers defaults, anticipation and autonomy?
test.explain: Written for complex interaction in complex UIs.

test.q: What should a heuristic finding include?
options: A reference to the original paper
test.explain: Naming the violation is only the start.
